obligations.text: A filesystem repository offers every module whose module.xml is found under its folder down to the configured depth.
obligations.cases: entry within depth vs deeper than depth; Depth=0 (unlimited) vs Depth=1 over a hidden .modules folder

obligations.text: IPM reads the folder into the cache on creation and on refresh; a refresh replaces the whole cache, so a module whose folder is gone stops being offered.
obligations.cases: new repository vs refresh of existing; module still present vs removed before refresh
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70 (owners_native.rs neighbour assertions native_109-115 exercise creation and the removed key 2)

obligations.text: A module.xml that is not a readable manifest is skipped and the rest are cached.
obligations.cases: unreadable vs valid manifest in one scan

obligations.text: A readable manifest whose module name is invalid fails the whole refresh, which then changes nothing.
obligations.cases: invalid name within scan depth vs beyond scan depth; failed vs successful build

obligations.text: A refresh of an existing repository locks it; while another process holds the lock the refresh fails (after a timeout) and changes nothing.
obligations.cases: foreign lock held vs free on an existing repository

obligations.text: The default refresh lock manager releases the explicit lock when the refresh method returns, even inside an outer transaction; explicit %New(0) keeps it through close until commit, default %New(1) releases at close.
obligations.cases: immediate (default) vs deferred lock manager; outer transaction depth 0 vs >0; before vs after commit
obligations.observation: lock held after return / after commit
obligations.basis: reused:package-sources metadata (corrected binding, iter2 boundaries withdrawal OW-CONSTRUCTOR)

obligations.text: The cache still needs consistent replacement: a competing refresh or writer must not observe or produce a mixed cache while a refresh is uncommitted.
obligations.cases: two concurrent refreshes / refresh plus writer under IRIS isolation vs a single refresh
obligations.observation: cache rows seen by each process
obligations.gap: No model of concurrent refreshes. owners.rs/boundaries.rs model one refresh with a foreign-lock Boolean. Missing contrast: process A purges and rebuilds Repo/Filesystem/Definition.cls::BuildCache rows inside an open transaction after the default lock is released at return, while process B refreshes or reads ^IPM.Repo.Filesystem.CacheD; the reader (SearchRepositoriesForModule) must see either old or new cache, never a mix. Open question repo.filesystem.concurrent-refresh.

obligations.text: Working assumption (intended): a module with an invalid name should be skipped with a warning, like an unreadable manifest, so the other modules stay available.
obligations.cases: invalid-name manifest alongside a valid one
obligations.observation: refresh status and the valid module's cache row
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70 (as-built model: an InvalidName entry fails the whole build and preserves the old rows, contradicting the intended skip)

parent.entailment: The parent owns the scan, refresh, lock and invalid-manifest rules and is graded directly; B6 only points to the children. No obligation is credited by composition.

units.B5: excluded: scope of the availability probe (not proof that authentication, pull or publish work) and evidence statement (native loopback cases)

obligations.text: An ORAS registry can use a registry namespace, a path inside the registry, when addressing packages.
obligations.cases: registry with vs without a namespace path
obligations.observation: request URL / tag reference used for pull and publish
obligations.gap: No model of ORAS reference construction (Repo/Oras/PackageService.cls and Definition namespace property). admission.rs folds the namespace into an abstract repository_path integer for the proposed contract only. Missing contrast: same module pulled from a definition with Namespace="ns" vs empty, observing the reference passed to the ORAS client.

obligations.text: ORAS repositories support Basic and token authentication.
obligations.cases: username/password vs token vs none
obligations.observation: credentials attached to the ORAS client request
obligations.gap: No model of ORAS credential attachment. iter2 registry.rs auth_status/token_probe classify probe replies, not which credential the ORAS client sends. Missing contrast: a registry requiring a token accepts the pull when a token is configured and refuses it with only Basic, observed at the registry request log.

obligations.text: IPM finds a module in an ORAS registry by its name or its external name.
obligations.cases: lookup by Name vs ExternalName vs neither
obligations.gap: No model of ORAS name resolution. thin_surfaces.rs::inspection_choice covers ModuleSummary.Show name/external-name selection, not the ORAS package lookup. Missing contrast: package published under the external name, install by Name vs by ExternalName at Repo/Oras/PackageService lookup.

obligations.text: ORAS errors name the repository and show the registry status and message.
obligations.cases: registry error vs success
obligations.gap: No model of ORAS error rendering; only native observation. Missing contrast: a failing ORAS call produces an error whose text contains the repository name and the registry HTTP status and message.

obligations.text: The ORAS availability adapter accepts a 2xx reply or a 401 carrying WWW-Authenticate; a headerless 401 and a 403 are unavailable.
obligations.cases: 200 vs 401+header vs 401 without header vs 403; transport failure

obligations.text: Working assumption: ORAS unpublish R/M V deletes the plain tag and every V__<platform> tag of that version.
obligations.cases: version with plain and platform tags
obligations.gap: No model of ORAS unpublish tag enumeration. iter2 registry.rs delete_prefix/delete_all only show sequential delete prefixes and the all-versions flag. Missing contrast: version 1.0.0 with tags 1.0.0 and 1.0.0__2026.1; after unpublish R/M 1.0.0 neither tag remains (open question repo.oras.unpublish-platform-policy).

obligations.text: Working assumption: changing an ORAS registry address clears its stored credentials, as for a remote registry.
obligations.cases: address changed vs unchanged on repo -modify
obligations.gap: No model of the ORAS definition update clearing credentials. Missing contrast: repo -oras -n R -url <new> keeps vs clears stored credentials compared with the same command with an unchanged URL (open question repo.oras.credentials-change-policy).

obligations.text: Archive validation skips non-tar layers and compares size and digest with the first tar layer; a later matching tar layer does not rescue an earlier mismatch.
obligations.cases: first tar mismatching then matching; non-tar before matching tar; first tar matching

obligations.text: The pull path chooses the first downloaded *.tgz, which need not name the same artifact as the validated first tar layer.
obligations.cases: two .tgz files whose first differs from the first tar layer
obligations.observation: archive file handed to the loader vs layer validated
obligations.gap: registry.rs::pull takes archive_found as one Boolean and verify_layers checks layer metadata separately; no rule links the selected file (first *.tgz in PackageService.cls::Pull) with the validated layer. Missing contrast: layers [tar A, tar B] with files B.tgz listed first; validation passes on A while the loader receives B.

obligations.text: Failed validation returns an error even if the raw helper assigned a stream.
obligations.cases: hash ok vs hash failed with stream linked

obligations.text: The final GetModule reader throws the failed status instead of returning the stream to the loader.
obligations.cases: failed vs passed validation
obligations.observation: archive released to loader; loader entered

obligations.text: As built, the ORAS client can unpack a directory layer in its staging area before IPM checks the package archive.
obligations.cases: size mismatch with a provider that extracts before IPM validation
obligations.gap: Trace.provider_extracts is a provider input, so the model shows only that IPM does not gate it (control provider-unpacks-only-after-validation rejected). That the bundled oras-py client extracts before PackageService.cls::VerifyModuleHashAndSize runs is native evidence only. Missing: a model of the client pull step ordering (download, extract directory layer, return) relative to the IPM hash/size check.

obligations.text: A failed archive size or digest check stops IPM from replacing the installed module's directory.
obligations.cases: size/digest mismatch vs match on a writable installed root

obligations.text: In a same-version reinstall with a size mismatch, the installed files, callable code and module row stay at the original revision and IPM records a failed, uncommitted install.
obligations.cases: size mismatch reinstall vs successful reinstall
obligations.observation: module record, callable code, history row Success/Committed
obligations.gap: as_built.rs observes only archive_released/loader_entered/installed_root_replaced. The module record (%IPM.Storage.Module), callable code and the history row written by HistoryTemp/AbstractHistory Finalize (Success=0, Committed=0) are native observations. Missing contrast: the same reinstall with matching vs mismatching size, observing ModuleD version and the history row's Success/Committed fields.

obligations.text: ORAS dependency resolution reads the manifest annotation by tag and retrieves the archive by tag again, so a tag moved between the two reads installs revision 2 after resolving with revision 1, and the archive passes the later size/digest check against revision 2.
obligations.cases: metadata manifest == pull manifest vs moved tag
obligations.basis: reused:package-sources metadata (iter68 as_built.rs; control hash-check-binds-earlier-metadata rejected)

obligations.text: Proposed (issue #281): when verification is configured for an ORAS repository, IPM must verify the publisher's authorization for the selected artifact (target, policy, signer, manifest digest) before unpacking it.
obligations.cases: authorized evidence for this target/policy/manifest vs missing, rejected, unavailable or mismatched evidence
obligations.basis: reused:package-sources metadata (iter68 admission.rs, 8 verified, 11 controls rejected). Design contract only: the pinned product has no verifier or configuration, so this grades the proposed rule, not product behaviour

obligations.text: Proposed: dependencies resolved from protected repositories use metadata and bytes from the same authorized manifest.
obligations.cases: resolution and admission with same vs different target/policy/manifest digest

obligations.text: Proposed: failed verification stops before unpacking or replacing the installed directory; verified metadata with bad bytes allows only metadata use.
obligations.cases: unauthorized vs authorized with bad bytes vs authorized with verified bytes
obligations.basis: reused:package-sources metadata (iter68 admission.rs; controls extraction-before-admission, root-replacement-before-admission, trust-outage-allows-metadata rejected)

obligations.text: Proposed: each admission decision is scoped to the selected repository and policy revision; cached evidence for another target, policy revision or manifest digest is not reused.
obligations.cases: old vs new target/policy/manifest digest
obligations.basis: reused:package-sources metadata (iter68 admission.rs; control reuse-old-policy-revision rejected). Open decisions in B2 (trust format, signer policy, unprotected fallback) are not graded
